memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then take all the fat on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar. But burn the bull's flesh and its hide and its intestines outside the camp. It is a sin offering." - Exodus 29:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Part of the sin offering was burned on the altar, but the rest — the flesh, the hide, the intestines — was carried outside the camp and burned there. The sin offering did not remain in the holy place. It was taken out, away from the community, and consumed beyond the boundary.

The writer of Hebrews notices this exact detail and draws a striking connection. He observes that the bodies of sin offerings were burned outside the camp, and then says: "And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood" (Heb 13:11-12). Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem's walls — put out, rejected, bearing sin beyond the boundary.

There is comfort here for anyone who has felt cast out. Jesus knows what it is to be put outside, excluded, treated as unwanted. He went there deliberately, and He went there for you. Hebrews then adds an invitation: let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore (Heb 13:13). Following Christ sometimes means standing where the crowd does not stand. But you never stand there alone; He is already outside the gate.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have I experienced rejection or exclusion that Christ understands from the inside?
Am I willing to be identified with Christ even when it costs me acceptance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You suffered outside the gate, rejected, so that I could be brought in. Thank You for going where I could not follow. Give me courage to stand with You. Amen.
